arcName: NDP 2026: The Show Must Go On

questions.title: The Debrief
questions.storyContext: 8:15pm. Last firework fades. Ops room dashboards are green for the first time all day. You survived the build, the crash, the wipe, the meltdown. The committee chair sits down: "I want to know what really happened."
questions.facilitatorPrompt: Do we tell her everything, or keep it clean? What if she hears it from someone else later?

options.label: Tell her everything — the 2am call, the crashes, the wipe, the stream nearly dying. Better it comes from us.
options.consequence: She listens in silence, then nods: "Thank you for trusting me with that." Your budget doubles next year.

options.label: Keep it professional: the app ran, minor adjustments made. She doesn't need to know how close it was.
options.consequence: The meeting is smooth and short. Then a contractor's group chat leaks. She calls again — colder this time.

options.label: Share the problems, framed as lessons learned. Not a damage report — a resilience report.
options.consequence: "Hit four times and kept standing," she repeats, writing it down. Your framing just became her framing.

options.label: Show the numbers: 99.2% [[uptime]], 40,000 served, positive social buzz after fireworks. Let the data speak.
options.consequence: She studies the charts, then looks up: "Nice numbers. But what happened at 1:30pm?" She already knows.

questions.title: One Shot
questions.storyContext: A week later, the Minister calls your team in. Three crises in three weeks for a national event. "I can fund one investment over five years to make sure this never happens again. What do you want?"
questions.facilitatorPrompt: One shot. What was the real root cause across everything we faced? Which fix prevents the most damage?

options.label: A permanent command centre for national events — dedicated systems, dedicated team, year-round standby.
options.consequence: Two years later, the F1 weekend app wobbles at 8pm — and a standing team catches it by 8:03.

options.label: An AI that predicts failures, scales up automatically, and blocks dangerous actions before they cause damage.
options.consequence: Eighteen months in, the AI blocks a sleepy admin from wiping the wrong database. Sound familiar?

options.label: Rebuild as fifty small pieces instead of one big app. No single failure can bring everything down.
options.consequence: Next year a payment module dies mid-parade — and nobody notices, because the other 49 pieces keep humming.

options.label: Train 200 digital officers across government with crisis playbooks. Technology breaks — people saved us every time.
options.consequence: Next crisis, a ministry you've never met handles it alone — using the playbook with your team's name on page one.
